title: Comparison 2 · Compare filter edges (TopHat vs Gaussian)
summary: Two filters with the same cutoff but different edge shapes. Visualise the frequency response and the real-space ringing side-by-side.

steps.title: Compare low-pass edges (how the frequency cut is shaped)
steps.body:
Same cutoff, different frequency-edge shape → very different real-space results:

  • `tophat` — rectangular window; 1.0 below fc, 0.0 above. Sharpest cut, but real-space suffers from **ringing** (Gibbs bands around edges).
  • `gauss`  — smooth `exp(-(f/fc)²/2)` decay. Zero ringing, but a touch of low-frequency softening.

In this tutorial we drop **two `filter.lp` nodes** side by side, set one to `kind=tophat` and the other to `kind=gauss`, and run the same input through both. One node supports all 5 filter shapes via its `kind` dropdown — no need to swap node types.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Siemens Star**. The radial wedges go higher-frequency toward the centre, so you can see 'where it was cut' at a glance. Sharp wedge boundaries (light→dark edges) also make **ringing visible as fringes**.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.siemens` shows its image before filtering.

steps.title: Drop the first Low-pass node
steps.body:
The Filter category contains just **`Filter · Low-pass`** and **`Filter · High-pass`** (the old separate TopHat / Gaussian / Fermi / … nodes are all folded into the `kind` dropdown inside Low-pass).

Drag **Filter · Low-pass** onto the canvas. We'll point this one at TopHat later (filter-shape switching happens in the Inspector's `kind` dropdown, not the palette).

steps.title: Wire Siemens → Low-pass #1
steps.body: Drag Siemens Star's `image` output to Low-pass #1's `image` input.

steps.title: Click Low-pass #1
steps.body: Click Low-pass #1. Core params: `kind` (filter shape), `fc` (cutoff in cycles/pixel; 0.5 = Nyquist), and `padding`. Extra params (`temp` or `fp`/`fs`) appear conditionally based on `kind`.

steps.title: Set kind to tophat (this one is the TopHat side)
steps.body: Change the `kind` dropdown to **`tophat`**. Low-pass #1 becomes a rectangular-window TopHat; the response plot should show a rectangle (1 below fc, 0 above).

steps.title: Lower fc to 0.08
steps.body: Enter **0.08** in `fc`. A fairly strong low-pass that makes both the cut and the ringing easy to see.

steps.title: Drop the second Low-pass node
steps.body: Drag another **Filter · Low-pass** next to Low-pass #1 — this will be the Gaussian side. We leave its `kind` at the default `gauss`, so no param tweak needed on the dropdown.

steps.title: Wire Siemens → Low-pass #2
steps.body: From the **same** Siemens Star's `image` output, drag to the new Low-pass #2's `image` input. The same input flows through both filters in parallel.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `filter.lp`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline — the Gaussian side has already run — before we match its fc to TopHat.

steps.title: Click Low-pass #2
steps.body: Click the new Low-pass #2. Leave `kind` at the default `gauss` — the response plot should now be a smooth bell curve (compare with TopHat's rectangle).

steps.title: Set fc to 0.08 (same cutoff)
steps.body: Enter **0.08** — same fc as TopHat, so only the shape differs.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. Both Low-passes execute and show their result previews. Lay them side-by-side — the centres look similarly blurred, but look closely at the wedge edges:

  • TopHat — **ring-shaped fringes** (ringing) hug each edge.
  • Gaussian — edges transition smoothly, zero rings.

Click to zoom for extra clarity.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
A sharp cutoff costs you ringing in real space (= rectangular-window-in-frequency ↔ sinc-convolution in real space). Gaussian is Gaussian in both domains → least artifact, so it's the default low-pass choice in cryo-EM.

**Next steps:** Change `kind` to `fermi` to reveal the `temp` parameter. Sweep `temp` from 0.001 (≈ TopHat) → 0.05 → 0.2 (≈ Gaussian) for a continuous sharpness knob. `butter` / `raised_cos` take two-band specs via `fp` / `fs`.
